bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷七十四 唐書50: 列傳26 康延孝 朱守殷 楊立 竇廷琬 張虔釗 楊彥溫
title.en: Volume 74 Book of Later Tang 50: Biographies 126 - Kang Yanxiao, Zhu Shouyin, Yang Li, Dou Tingwan, Zhang Qianzhao, Yang Yanwen
title.raw: 卷七十四 唐書50: 列傳26 康延孝 朱守殷 楊立 竇廷琬 張虔釗 楊彥溫 Volume 74 Book of Later Tang 50: Biographies 126 - Kang Yanxiao, Zhu Shouyin, Yang Li, Dou Tingwan, Zhang Qianzhao, Yang Yanwen

sentences.zh: 三年，討蜀，以延孝為西南行營馬步軍先鋒、排陣斬斫等使。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Shu was attacked, Yanxiao was appointed Vanguard of the Horse and Foot Forces of the Southwest Campaign Headquarters, Commissioner for Battle Formation and Cutting Down, and other such posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, during the campaign against Shu, Yanxiao was made vanguard of the southwest expedition's combined cavalry and infantry, with additional titles for assault and battle-formation duties.

sentences.zh: 延孝性驍健，徇利奮不顧身。

translations.literal: Yanxiao's nature was fierce and robust; pursuing gain, he strove forward without regard for his person.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao was by nature bold and hardy, and in pursuit of advantage he fought without thought for his own safety.

sentences.zh: 以前鋒下鳳州，收固鎮，降興州，敗王衍軍於三泉，所俘蜀軍皆諭而釋之，自是晝夜兼行。

translations.literal: As vanguard he descended on Feng Prefecture, recovered Gu Town, received the surrender of Xing Prefecture, and defeated Wang Yan's army at Sanquan; all Shu soldiers captured he instructed and released, and from then on marched day and night without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the vanguard, he took Feng Prefecture, recovered Gu Town, accepted the surrender of Xing Prefecture, and routed Wang Yan's forces at Sanquan. Every Shu soldier he captured he reasoned with and set free, and from that point he pressed forward day and night.

sentences.zh: 王衍自利州奔歸成都，斷吉柏津浮梁，以絕諸軍。

translations.literal: Wang Yan fled from Lizhou back to Chengdu, severed the pontoon bridge at Jibo Ford, and thereby cut off the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan fled from Lizhou to Chengdu, cut the pontoon bridge at Jibo Ford, and thereby blocked the advancing armies.

sentences.zh: 延孝復造浮梁以渡，進收綿州，王衍復斷綿江浮梁而去。

translations.literal: Yanxiao again built a pontoon bridge to cross, advanced and took Mian Prefecture; Wang Yan again severed the pontoon bridge on the Mian River and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao built another pontoon bridge to cross, advanced and seized Mian Prefecture, and Wang Yan in turn cut the Mian River bridge and retreated.

sentences.zh: 水深無舟楫可渡，延孝謂招撫使李嚴曰：「吾懸軍深入，利在急兵。

translations.literal: The water was deep and there were no boats or oars by which to cross. Yanxiao said to the Pacification Commissioner Li Yan: "I have led an isolated army deep into enemy territory; the advantage lies in pressing the attack swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: The river ran too deep for boats, and Yanxiao told the pacification commissioner Li Yan, "I have driven a detached force deep into hostile country; our advantage lies in speed.

sentences.zh: 乘王衍破膽之時，人心離沮，但得百騎過鹿頭關，彼即迎降不暇。

translations.literal: Seizing the moment when Wang Yan's courage is broken and men's hearts are scattered and dejected, if we can get even a hundred horsemen past Lutou Pass, they will have no leisure but to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Yan is still terrified and his people's morale is collapsing, a mere hundred horsemen through Lutou Pass will leave them scrambling to surrender.

sentences.zh: 如俟修繕津梁，便留數日，若王衍堅閉近關，折吾兵勢，儻延旬浹，則勝負莫可知也，宜促騎渡江。

translations.literal: If we wait to repair the ford and bridge, we will linger several days; if Wang Yan firmly closes the nearby passes and blunts our army's momentum, and should it drag on for ten days and more, then victory and defeat cannot be known—we ought to urge the cavalry to cross the river at once.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait to rebuild the crossing, we lose days; if Wang Yan seals the nearby passes and breaks our momentum, and the campaign drags on another ten days, the outcome becomes uncertain. We must get the cavalry across the river now.

sentences.zh: 」因與李嚴乘馬浮江，於是得濟者僅千人，步軍溺死者亦千餘人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he and Li Yan rode their horses across the floating river; of those who got across, barely a thousand, while of the infantry who drowned, again more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " He and Li Yan then rode their horses across the river. Only about a thousand men made it over, while more than a thousand foot soldiers drowned.

sentences.zh: 延孝既濟，長驅通鹿頭，進據漢州。

translations.literal: Once Yanxiao had crossed, he drove at full speed through Lutou and advanced to occupy Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once across, Yanxiao drove straight through Lutou Pass and seized Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 居三日，部下後軍方至。

translations.literal: After three days' stay, the rear army of his subordinates only then arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, his rear guard finally caught up.

sentences.zh: 偽蜀六軍使王宗弼令人持牛酒幣馬歸款。

translations.literal: The bogus-Shu Six Armies Commissioner Wang Zongbi sent men bearing cattle, wine, silks, and horses to submit allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongbi, the Six Armies commissioner of the Shu regime, sent envoys with cattle, wine, silks, and horses to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 旬日，兩川平定，延孝止漢州以俟繼岌。

translations.literal: Within ten days, the Two Rivers were pacified; Yanxiao halted at Han Prefecture to await Jiji.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days both river circuits were pacified, and Yanxiao held Han Prefecture to await Jiji.

sentences.zh: 平蜀之功，延孝居最。

translations.literal: Among the achievements in pacifying Shu, Yanxiao ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Shu, Yanxiao's merit stood first.

sentences.zh: 時邠州節度使董璋為行營右廂馬步使，華州節度使毛璋為行營左廂馬步使，以軍禮當事延孝。

translations.literal: At that time Bin Prefecture Military Governor Dong Zhang served as Right Wing Horse and Foot Commissioner of the campaign headquarters, and Hua Prefecture Military Governor Mao Zhang as Left Wing Horse and Foot Commissioner; by military etiquette they were subordinate to Yanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Dong Zhang, military governor of Bin, was right-wing horse-and-foot commander of the expedition, and Mao Zhang of Hua was left-wing commander; by military protocol both answered to Yanxiao.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜以私愛董璋，及西川平定之後，崇韜每有兵機，必召璋參決，延孝不平。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao favored Dong Zhang privately; after the Western River Circuit was pacified, whenever Chongtao had military plans he invariably summoned Zhang to join in deciding them, and Yanxiao was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao favored Dong Zhang personally, and after western Sichuan was pacified he consulted Zhang on every military matter. Yanxiao resented it.

sentences.zh: 時延孝軍於城西，毛璋軍於城東，董璋軍於城中。

translations.literal: At that time Yanxiao's army was west of the city, Mao Zhang's east of the city, and Dong Zhang's within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao camped west of the city, Mao Zhang east of it, and Dong Zhang inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 閏十二月，延孝因酒酣謂董璋曰：「吾有平蜀之功，公等仆蔌相從，反首鼠於侍中之門，謀相傾陷，吾為都將，公乃裨校，力能斬首。

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month, Yanxiao, flushed with wine, said to Dong Zhang: "I have the achievement of pacifying Shu; you and the rest followed like trailing weeds, yet you waver like a rat at the Vice Director's gate, plotting to overthrow me. I am the chief commander and you are but a lieutenant—I have the strength to cut off your head.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month, Yanxiao, drunk, told Dong Zhang, "I won Shu. You lot tagged along like weeds, yet you scurry between loyalties at the Vice Director's door and plot against me. I am commander-in-chief and you a subordinate—I could take your head.

sentences.zh: 」璋惶恐，謝之而退。

translations.literal: " Zhang was terrified, apologized, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang, terrified, apologized and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 酒罷，璋訴於郭崇韜，崇韜陰銜之，乃署董璋為東川節度使，落軍職。

translations.literal: When the drinking ended, Zhang complained to Guo Chongtao; Chongtao secretly harbored resentment toward Yanxiao, and thereupon appointed Dong Zhang Military Governor of Eastern River Circuit and removed him from army duties.
translations.idiomatic: After the banquet Zhang appealed to Guo Chongtao, who secretly took offense at Yanxiao and appointed Dong Zhang military governor of the eastern circuit, removing him from the army command.

sentences.zh: 延孝怒，謂毛璋曰：「吾冒白刃，犯險阻，平定兩川，董璋何功，遽有其地！

translations.literal: Yanxiao was angry and said to Mao Zhang: "I braved naked blades and braved perilous passes to pacify the Two Rivers—what achievement has Dong Zhang that he should suddenly have that territory!
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao, furious, said to Mao Zhang, "I faced blades and hardship to conquer both circuits—what has Dong Zhang done to deserve that land!

sentences.zh: 」二人因謁見崇韜，曰：「東川重地，宜擇良帥，工部任尚書有文武才幹，甚洽眾心，請表為東川帥。

translations.literal: " The two men thereupon had an audience with Chongtao and said: "Eastern River Circuit is a weighty post and ought to have a worthy commander; the Minister of Works, Vice Director Ren, has civil and military talent and is greatly in accord with the people's hearts—we request a memorial appointing him commander of Eastern River Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " The two then saw Chongtao and said, "Eastern Sichuan is too important for Dong Zhang. Minister Ren has both civil and military ability and the troops' trust; we ask that he be named its commander.

sentences.zh: 」崇韜怒曰：「紹琛反耶？

translations.literal: " Chongtao said angrily: "Has Shaochen rebelled?
translations.idiomatic: " Chongtao snapped, "Has Shaochen turned rebel?

sentences.zh: 敢違吾節度！

translations.literal: He dares defy my command!
translations.idiomatic: How dare he defy my orders!

sentences.zh: 」延孝等惶恐而退。

translations.literal: " Yanxiao and the others withdrew in fear.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanxiao and the others withdrew in alarm.

sentences.zh: 未幾，崇韜為繼岌所害，二人因責董璋曰：「公復首鼠何門？

translations.literal: Before long, Chongtao was killed by Jiji; the two men thereupon reproached Dong Zhang, saying: "To which door will you waver like a rat again?
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Chongtao was killed on Jiji's orders, and the two confronted Dong Zhang: "Which door will you run to now?

sentences.zh: 」璋俯首祈哀而已。

translations.literal: " Zhang only bowed his head and pleaded for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang could only bow his head and beg for mercy.

sentences.zh: 四年正月甲申，大軍發成都，繼岌令延孝以一萬二千人為後軍。

translations.literal: On the first month, day jiashen, of the fourth year, the great army set out from Chengdu; Jiji ordered Yanxiao to take twelve thousand men as the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the first month of the fourth year, the main army left Chengdu, with Yanxiao commanding twelve thousand men as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 二月癸巳，中軍次武連，中使詔至，諭以西平王朱友謙有罪伏誅，命繼岌殺其子遂州節度使令德，延孝大驚。

translations.literal: On the second month, day guisi, the central army halted at Wulian; an imperial envoy's edict arrived, announcing that the Prince of Xiping, Zhu Youqian, had been executed for his crime and ordering Jiji to kill his son, Suizhou Military Governor Lingde; Yanxiao was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in the second month the main force reached Wulian. An imperial messenger arrived with orders that Zhu Youqian, Prince of Xiping, had been executed for treason and that Jiji must kill his son Lingde, military governor of Suizhou. Yanxiao was stunned.

sentences.zh: 俄而董璋率兵之遂州，遇延孝不謁，延孝怒，謂諸校曰：「南平梁汴，西定巴邛，畫策之謀，始於郭公，而汗馬之勞，力摧強敵，即吾也。

translations.literal: Shortly Dong Zhang led troops to Suizhou; meeting Yanxiao he did not pay a visit, and Yanxiao was angry. He said to the commanders: "Pacifying Liang and Bian in the south and securing Ba and Qiong in the west—the stratagems began with Lord Guo, but the sweat of battle and the labor of crushing strong foes—that was me.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dong Zhang marched to Suizhou and, meeting Yanxiao, did not call on him. Yanxiao raged at his officers: "We pacified Liang and Bian in the south and secured Ba and Qiong in the west. Guo Chongtao planned it, but the fighting that broke the enemy—that was me.

sentences.zh: 若以背偽歸國，犄角而成霸業，即西平王之功第一。

translations.literal: If one speaks of turning from a false regime to serve the true state and forming pincers to achieve hegemony, then the Prince of Xiping's merit ranks first.
translations.idiomatic: If merit lies in abandoning a false master to serve the throne and helping build the empire, the Prince of Xiping stood first.

sentences.zh: 西平與郭公皆以無罪赤族，歸朝之後，次當及我矣！

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiping and Lord Guo were both exterminated root and branch though guiltless; after returning to court, next it will reach me!
translations.idiomatic: Xiping and Guo were wiped out though innocent. After we return to court, I will be next!

sentences.zh: 」丙申，延孝次劍州。

translations.literal: " On day bingshen, Yanxiao halted at Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " On bingshen, Yanxiao reached Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時延孝部下皆鄜、延、河中舊將，焦武等知西平王被禍，兼誅令德，號哭軍門，訴於延孝曰：「西平無罪，二百口伏誅，河中舊將，無不從坐，某等必死矣！

translations.literal: At that time Yanxiao's subordinates were all old generals from Fu, Yan, and Hezhong; Jiao Wu and others, learning the Prince of Xiping had suffered calamity and that Lingde was also executed, wailed at the army gate and appealed to Yanxiao: "The Prince of Xiping was guiltless, yet two hundred mouths were put to death; of the old generals of Hezhong, none escape implication—we are certain to die!
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao's officers were veterans from Fu, Yan, and Hezhong. When Jiao Wu and others learned of Xiping's death and Lingde's execution, they wept at the camp gate and told Yanxiao, "Xiping was innocent, yet two hundred of his kin were killed. Every old Hezhong officer will be implicated—we are dead men!

sentences.zh: 」時魏王繼岌到泥溪，延孝報繼岌云：「河中兵士號哭，欲為亂。

translations.literal: " At that time the Prince of Wei, Jiji, had reached Nixi; Yanxiao reported to Jiji: "The Hezhong soldiers are wailing and wish to make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Wei Jiji had reached Nixi. Yanxiao reported, "The Hezhong troops are wailing and may mutiny.

sentences.zh: 」丁酉，延孝至劍州，遂擁眾回，自稱西川節度、三川製置等使，以檄招諭蜀人，三日間，眾及五萬。

translations.literal: " On day dingyou, Yanxiao reached Jian Prefecture, then led the masses in turning back, styled himself Military Governor of Western River Circuit, Commissioner for Administration of the Three Rivers, and other such titles, and by proclamation summoned and instructed the Shu people; within three days his followers reached fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " On dingyou he reached Jian Prefecture, turned his force around, and declared himself military governor of western Sichuan and commissioner for the three river circuits. Within three days his proclamations had rallied fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 己亥，繼岌至利州。

translations.literal: On day jihai, Jiji reached Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Jiji reached Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是夜，守吉柏津使密告魏王曰：「得紹琛文字，令斷吉柏浮梁。

translations.literal: That night the officer guarding Jibo Ford secretly reported to the Prince of Wei: "I have obtained Shaochen's written order to sever the Jibo pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: That night the officer at Jibo Ford secretly warned the prince, "I have a message from Shaochen ordering the Jibo bridge cut.

sentences.zh: 」繼岌懼，乃令梁漢顒以兵控吉柏津。

translations.literal: " Jiji was afraid and thereupon ordered Liang Hanyong to take troops and secure Jibo Ford.
translations.idiomatic: " Alarmed, Jiji sent Liang Hanyong to seize the ford.

sentences.zh: 延孝已擁眾急趨西川，繼岌遣人馳書諭之。

translations.literal: Yanxiao had already led the masses in haste toward Western River Circuit; Jiji sent a man with urgent letters to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao was already racing west with his army, and Jiji sent urgent letters ordering him to stop.

sentences.zh: 夜半，令監軍使李廷安召任圜，因署為副招討使。

translations.literal: At midnight he ordered the Army Supervisor Li Ting'an to summon Ren Huan and thereupon appointed him Deputy Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he had the army supervisor Li Ting'an summon Ren Huan and appoint him deputy pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 令圜率兵七千騎，與都指揮使梁漢顒、監軍李廷安討之。

translations.literal: He ordered Huan to lead seven thousand horsemen, together with the Chief Commander Liang Hanyong and the Army Supervisor Li Ting'an, to attack Yanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan was to lead seven thousand cavalry, with chief commander Liang Hanyong and supervisor Li Ting'an, against Yanxiao.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，先令都將何建崇擊劍門，下之。

translations.literal: On day xinchou, he first ordered the Chief Commander He Jianchong to attack Jianmen Pass and take it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he sent chief commander He Jianchong to storm Jianmen Pass and take it.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，圜以大軍至漢州，延孝來逆戰，圜令董璋以東川懦卒當其鋒，伏精兵於其後，延孝擊退東川之兵，急追之，遇伏兵起，延孝敗，馳入漢州，閉壁不出。

translations.literal: On day jiayin, Huan with the great army reached Han Prefecture; Yanxiao came to meet him in battle. Huan ordered Dong Zhang to take the Eastern River Circuit's weak soldiers to meet the enemy's edge, with elite troops ambushed behind them. Yanxiao struck and repelled the Eastern River troops, pursued them hotly, met the ambush rising, was defeated, galloped into Han Prefecture, and closed the walls without coming out.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Ren Huan reached Han Prefecture with the main force. Yanxiao met him in battle. Ren Huan put Dong Zhang's weak eastern troops in the front line and hid elite troops behind them. Yanxiao routed the eastern force and pursued recklessly into the ambush. Defeated, he fled into Han Prefecture and shut the gates.

sentences.zh: 西川孟知祥以兵二萬，與圜合勢攻之。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang of Western River Circuit, with twenty thousand troops, joined forces with Huan to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang of western Sichuan brought twenty thousand men to join Ren Huan's assault.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·李延厚傳》：康延孝入漢州，知祥遣延厚率兵二千會李仁罕討之，將行，誓士卒曰：「今出師不三旬必破賊，乃立功圖賞之日也。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Li Yanhou in the 《Records of the Nine States》: When Kang Yanxiao entered Han Prefecture, Zhixiang sent Yanhou leading two thousand troops to join Li Renhan in attacking him. About to set out, he swore to the soldiers: "On this campaign, within thirty days we shall surely break the bandits—this is the day to achieve merit and seek reward.
translations.idiomatic: (From Li Yanhou's biography in the 《Records of the Nine States》: When Kang Yanxiao entered Han Prefecture, Zhixiang sent Yanhou with two thousand men to join Li Renhan. Before marching, he swore to his troops, "We will break the rebels within thirty days. This is the day to win merit and reward.

sentences.zh: 士卒忠奮者立東廂，衰疾者立西廂，無自苦也。

translations.literal: Soldiers loyal and ardent, stand in the east wing; those weak and ill, stand in the west wing—do not torment yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Let the loyal and eager stand on the east side, the weak and sick on the west. Do not force yourselves.

sentences.zh: 」得請行者七百人，逐延孝西寨，斬首百餘級，竟拔其城。）〉

translations.literal: " Seven hundred men volunteered to go; they pursued Yanxiao's western stockade, cut off more than a hundred heads, and in the end stormed his fort.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Seven hundred volunteered, stormed Yanxiao's western camp, took more than a hundred heads, and finally captured the fort.)〉

sentences.zh: 漢州四面樹竹木為柵。

translations.literal: Han Prefecture on all four sides had bamboo and trees planted as palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Han Prefecture was ringed with palisades of bamboo and timber.

sentences.zh: 三月乙丑，圜陣於金雁橋，即率諸軍鼓噪而進，四面縱火，風焰亙空。

translations.literal: On the third month, day yichou, Huan formed battle lines at Golden Goose Bridge, then led the armies forward with drums and shouts, setting fires on all four sides; wind and flame filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the third month Ren Huan drew up at Golden Goose Bridge, led the armies forward with drums and shouts, and set fires on every side until flames filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 於是延孝危急，引騎出戰，遇陣於金雁橋，又敗之，以十數騎奔綿州；

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanxiao was in dire straits; he led his horsemen out to fight, met the battle line at Golden Goose Bridge, was again defeated, and with a dozen-odd horsemen fled toward Mian Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao, desperate, led his cavalry out, was beaten again at Golden Goose Bridge, and fled toward Mian Prefecture with only a dozen horsemen;

sentences.zh: 何建崇追及，擒之，任圜命載以檻車。

translations.literal: He Jianchong overtook and captured him; Ren Huan ordered him loaded into a caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: He Jianchong overtook and captured him, and Ren Huan had him placed in a cage cart.

sentences.zh: 時孟知祥與任圜、董璋置酒高會，因引令延孝檻車至會。

translations.literal: At that time Meng Zhixiang, together with Ren Huan and Dong Zhang, held a lofty banquet; they thereupon had Yanxiao in his caged cart brought to the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang was feasting with Ren Huan and Dong Zhang and had Yanxiao brought to the banquet in his cage cart.

sentences.zh: 知祥問曰：「明公頃自梁朝脫身歸命，才平汴水，節制陝郊，近領前鋒，克平劍外，歸朝之後，授爵冊勳，巨鎮尊官，誰與為競！

translations.literal: Zhixiang asked: "Your Excellency not long ago escaped from the Liang court to submit to our mandate; you had just pacified the Bian waters, governed Shaan and the suburbs, lately led the vanguard and conquered the lands beyond Jian—after returning to court, titles and merit registers were bestowed, great prefectures and honored offices—who could rival you!
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang asked, "You left the Liang court to serve the throne, pacified Bian, governed Shaan, led the vanguard and conquered the lands beyond Jian, and on your return received titles, honors, and a great command. Who could rival you!

sentences.zh: 奈何躁憤，自毀功庸，入此檻車，還為鄧艾，深可痛惜，誰肯湣之！

translations.literal: Why then be rash and resentful, destroying your own achievements, entering this caged cart, becoming again a Deng Ai—deeply to be lamented; who would pity you!
translations.idiomatic: Why then let anger destroy your achievements, end up in this cage, and become another Deng Ai? It is a bitter waste. Who will pity you now!

sentences.zh: 」知祥因手自注杯以飲之。

translations.literal: " Zhixiang thereupon personally filled a cup and had him drink.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhixiang filled a cup himself and had him drink.

sentences.zh: 延孝曰：「自知富貴難消，官職已足。

translations.literal: Yanxiao said: "I know myself that wealth and honor are hard to bear down; my offices were already sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao said, "I knew wealth and rank were more than I could bear, and my offices were enough.

sentences.zh: 然郭崇韜佐命元勳，輔成大業，不動干戈，收獲兩川，自古殊功，但恐不及，一旦何罪，闔門被誅；

translations.literal: Yet Guo Chongtao was a founding minister who aided the mandate, assisted in achieving the great enterprise, took the Two Rivers without drawing weapons—an extraordinary achievement since antiquity, perhaps unmatched—and in a single day, for what crime, his whole household was put to death;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guo Chongtao, a founding minister who helped build the empire and took both circuits without a battle—a feat perhaps unmatched in history—was executed with his entire household in a single day, for no crime anyone could name;

sentences.zh: 延孝之徒，何保首領。

translations.literal: How could men of Yanxiao's sort preserve their heads?
translations.idiomatic: How could men like me hope to keep our heads?

sentences.zh: 以此思慮，不敢歸朝，天道相違，一旦至此，亦其命也，夫復何言！

translations.literal: With this in mind I dared not return to court; Heaven's way opposed me, and in a single day I came to this—it is also my fate; what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: That is why I dared not return to court. Heaven turned against me, and in a day I came to this. It is fate. What more can I say!

sentences.zh: 」及圜班師，行次鳳翔，中使向延嗣齎詔至，遂誅之。

translations.literal: " When Huan withdrew the army and marched, halting at Fengxiang, the imperial envoy Xiang Yansi arrived bearing the edict, and Yanxiao was thereupon executed.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ren Huan withdrew and reached Fengxiang, the imperial envoy Xiang Yansi arrived with the execution order, and Yanxiao was put to death.

sentences.zh: 部下懷其首級，瘞於昭應縣民陳暉地。

translations.literal: His subordinates cherished his severed head and buried it on the land of Chen Hui, a commoner of Zhaoying County.
translations.idiomatic: His men kept his head and buried it on land belonging to Chen Hui, a commoner of Zhaoying County.

sentences.zh: 天成初，其子發之攜去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tiancheng reign, his son exhumed it and carried it away.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiancheng reign his son exhumed it and took it away.

sentences.zh: 朱守殷，小字會兒。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouyin, whose childhood name was Hui'er.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin, known in childhood as Hui'er.

sentences.zh: 莊宗就學，以廝養之役給事左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was pursuing his studies, he was assigned to menial service attending at his side.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuangzong was still a student, he served him in menial attendance.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗即位，為長直軍使，雖列戎行，不聞戰攻。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he became Chief of the Long-Service Guard; though ranked among the military, he was not known for battle or assault.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was made chief of the long-service guard. Though he held military rank, he was never known for fighting.

sentences.zh: 每構人之短長，中於莊宗，漸以心腹受委。

translations.literal: He constantly framed people's faults and merits so as to strike Zhuangzong's heart, and gradually was entrusted as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly played on others' faults and virtues to sway Zhuangzong and gradually became a trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 河上對壘，稍遷蕃漢馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: When the armies faced each other on the Yellow River, he was gradually promoted to Chief Adjutant of the Tribal and Han Horse and Foot Forces.
translations.idiomatic: During the standoff on the Yellow River he was promoted to chief adjutant of the combined tribal and Han forces.

sentences.zh: 守殷守德勝寨，為梁將王彥章所攻，守殷無備，遂陷南寨。

translations.literal: Shouyin defended Desheng Stockade; attacked by the Liang general Wang Yanzhang, Shouyin was unprepared, and the southern stockade fell.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyin held Desheng Stockade. The Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked it, and Shouyin, unprepared, lost the southern stockade.

sentences.zh: 莊宗聞之曰：「駑才大誤予事！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong heard of it and said: "This dull-witted fellow has greatly mistaken my affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said when he heard it, "That fool has ruined my campaign!

sentences.zh: 」因撤北寨，往固楊劉。

translations.literal: " He thereupon withdrew from the northern stockade and went to secure Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: " He withdrew from the northern stockade and went to secure Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 明宗在鄆州，密請以覆軍之罪罪之，莊宗私於腹心，忍而不問。

translations.literal: Mingzong was at Yan Prefecture and secretly requested that he be punished with the crime of destroying the army; Zhuangzong, privately regarding him as a confidant, bore it and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong, then at Yan Prefecture, privately asked that he be punished for losing the army, but Zhuangzong, treating him as a personal favorite, bore the fault and did nothing.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，為振武節度使，不之任，仍兼領蕃漢馬步軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang, he was made Military Governor of Zhenwu but did not take up the post, still concurrently commanding the Tribal and Han Horse and Foot Forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongguang he was named military governor of Zhenwu but never took up the post, while retaining command of the combined tribal and Han forces.

sentences.zh: 京城初定，內外警巡，恃憑主恩，蔑視勳舊，與景進互相表裏，又強作宿德之態，言語遲緩，自謂沉厚。

translations.literal: When the capital was first secured, he patrolled inside and outside; relying on the ruler's favor, he looked down on the meritorious elders, acted in concert with Jing Jin, and also forced a manner of long-standing virtue—his speech slow and deliberate, calling himself deep and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was first secured he took charge of internal and external patrols. Relying on imperial favor, he scorned the old meritocrats, worked hand in glove with Jing Jin, and affected the manner of a seasoned elder—slow of speech, calling himself grave and steady.

sentences.zh: 及郭從謙犯興教門，步軍始亂，中使急召騎士，守殷按甲不進，莊宗獨領宦官斫射，屢退，而騎軍終不至。

translations.literal: When Guo Congqian attacked Xingjiao Gate, the foot soldiers first fell into disorder; the palace envoy urgently summoned the horsemen, but Shouyin held his armor and did not advance. Zhuangzong alone led the eunuchs in hacking and shooting, repeatedly driven back, while the cavalry never arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Congqian attacked Xingjiao Gate and the infantry broke, palace envoys urgently summoned the cavalry, but Shouyin held his troops back. Zhuangzong alone led eunuchs in the fighting, was driven back again and again, and the cavalry never came.

sentences.zh: 莊宗既崩，守殷擁眾方在北邙，憩於茂林之下。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong had perished, Shouyin was leading the masses on North Mang, resting beneath a dense grove.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong's death Shouyin was encamped with his troops on North Mang, resting in a grove.

sentences.zh: 迨聞凶問，乃入內，選嬪御及珍寶以歸，恣軍士劫掠京都，翌日方定，率諸校迎明宗於東郊。

translations.literal: When he heard the news of death, he then entered within, selected palace women and precious objects to take away, let the soldiers plunder the capital at will; only the next day was order restored, and he led the commanders to welcome Mingzong at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the news he entered the palace, took consorts and treasures for himself, and let his troops loot the capital. Order was restored only the next day, when he led his officers to welcome Mingzong at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 天成初，授河南尹，判六軍諸衛事，加侍中，移汴州節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, he was appointed Intendant of Henan, with authority over the Six Armies and all guards, promoted to Palace Attendant, and transferred as Military Governor of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he was made intendant of Henan with authority over the Six Armies and guards, promoted to palace attendant, and transferred to military governor of Bian.

sentences.zh: 車駕將巡幸，外議喧然，初以為平吳，又云製置東諸侯。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to tour, outside talk was clamorous—at first it was thought to be pacifying Wu, then it was said to be arranging the eastern feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to go on tour, rumor ran wild—first that he would pacify Wu, then that he would reorganize the eastern lords.

sentences.zh: 守殷乃生雲夢之疑，遂殺都校馬彥超、副使宋敬。

translations.literal: Shouyin then conceived suspicions like those of the Duke of Yunmeng and thereupon killed Chief Commander Ma Yanchao and Deputy Commissioner Song Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyin, seized with paranoid suspicion, killed chief commander Ma Yanchao and deputy commissioner Song Jing.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》：守殷將叛，召都指揮使馬彥超與計事，彥超不從，守殷殺之。

translations.literal: (From the 《History of the Five Dynasties by Ouyang Xiu》: When Shouyin was about to rebel, he summoned the Chief Commander Ma Yanchao to discuss plans; Yanchao would not follow, and Shouyin killed him.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《History of the Five Dynasties by Ouyang Xiu》: When Shouyin was about to rebel he summoned chief commander Ma Yanchao to plot with him. Yanchao refused, and Shouyin killed him.

sentences.zh: 明宗憐彥超之死，以其子承祚為洺州長史。）〉

translations.literal: Mingzong pitied Yanchao's death and appointed his son Chengzuo Long Secretary of Luozhou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong pitied Yanchao and appointed his son Chengzuo long secretary of Luozhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 守殷驅市人閉壁以叛，明宗途次京水，聞之，親統禁軍，倍程直抵其壘，長圍夾攻，縋城甚眾。

translations.literal: Shouyin drove the townspeople to close the walls and rebel; Mingzong, on the road at Jingshui, heard of it, personally commanded the palace guard, doubled his pace straight to the fortress, laid a long siege with attacks from both sides, and many were lowered from the walls on ropes.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyin drove the townspeople to shut the walls and rebel. Mingzong, marching at Jingshui, heard the news, took personal command of the palace guard, raced to the city, laid siege from all sides, and many defenders were lowered on ropes.

sentences.zh: 守殷力屈，盡殺其族，引頸令左右盡其命。

translations.literal: Shouyin's strength was exhausted; he killed his entire clan, stretched out his neck, and ordered those at his side to end his life.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyin, exhausted, killed his entire clan, bared his neck, and ordered his attendants to finish him.

sentences.zh: 王師入城，索其黨，盡誅之。

translations.literal: The royal army entered the city, sought out his partisans, and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army entered the city, hunted down his followers, and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 詔鞭守殷屍，梟首懸於都市，滿七日，傳送洛陽。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shouyin's corpse flogged, his head cut off and hung in the market; after seven full days it was sent on to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his corpse flogged and his head displayed in the market. After seven days the head was sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 楊立者，潞州之小校。

translations.literal: Yang Li was a petty officer of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Li was a junior officer at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 初事李嗣昭及李繼韜，皆畜養甚厚。

translations.literal: He first served Li Sizhao and Li Jiyao; both raised and supported him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served Li Sizhao and Li Jiyao, both of whom treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 繼韜被誅，憤憤失誌。

translations.literal: When Jiyao was executed, he was resentful and lost his purpose.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiyao was executed, he grew bitter and lost heart.

sentences.zh: 同光二年四月，有詔以潞兵三萬人戍涿州，將發，其眾謀曰：「我輩事故使二十年，衣食豐足，未嘗邊塞征行，苟於邊上差跌，白骨何歸？

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Tongguang, an edict ordered thirty thousand Luzhou troops to garrison Zhuo Prefecture. About to set out, the masses plotted, saying: "We have served our old lord for twenty years, with ample food and clothing, and have never campaigned on the frontier. If we stumble on the border, to what home will our white bones return?
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Tongguang an edict ordered thirty thousand Luzhou troops to garrison Zhuo. Before they marched, the men plotted: "We served our old lord for twenty years in comfort and never fought on the frontier. If we fail out there, where will our bones lie?

sentences.zh: 不如據城自固，事成則富貴耳。

translations.literal: Better to hold the city and secure ourselves; if the affair succeeds, then wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold the city. If we succeed, we gain wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 」因聚徒百餘輩，攻子城東門，城中大擾。

translations.literal: " They thereupon gathered more than a hundred followers, attacked the inner city's east gate, and great turmoil arose within the city.
translations.idiomatic: " More than a hundred men gathered, stormed the inner east gate, and threw the city into chaos.

sentences.zh: 副使李繼珂及監軍張機祚出奔。

translations.literal: Deputy Commissioner Li Jike and Army Supervisor Zhang Jizuo fled.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioner Li Jike and army supervisor Zhang Jizuo fled.

sentences.zh: 立自稱留後，率軍民上表請旄節。

translations.literal: Li styled himself Acting Military Governor, led the army and people in submitting a memorial requesting the commander's banner and staff.
translations.idiomatic: Li declared himself acting military governor and led the troops and people in petitioning for the commander's banner and staff.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒，命明宗與李紹真攻討，一月拔之，生擒立及其同惡十餘人，送於闕下，皆磔於市。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was angry and ordered Mingzong and Li Shaozhen to attack and suppress them; within one month they took the city, captured Li alive together with more than ten fellow evildoers, sent them to the capital, and all were dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong, furious, ordered Mingzong and Li Shaozhen to attack them. Within a month the city fell. Li and more than ten accomplices were captured alive, sent to the capital, and dismembered in the market.

sentences.zh: 潞州城峻而隍深，攻立輒敢據之，莊宗因茲詔諸道撤防城之備焉。

translations.literal: Luzhou's walls were high and its moat deep; attacking Li, they still dared to hold it. Zhuangzong thereupon issued an edict to all circuits to dismantle their defensive preparations for cities.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou's walls were high and its moat deep, yet Li had dared to hold it. Zhuangzong then ordered all circuits to dismantle their city defenses.

sentences.zh: 竇廷琬者，世為青州牙將，梁祖擢置左右。

translations.literal: Dou Tingwan—his family for generations were military aides of Qing Prefecture; the Liang Founder promoted him and placed him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tingwan came from a family of military aides at Qing Prefecture. The Liang founder promoted him to personal attendance.

sentences.zh: 同光初，為復州遊奕使，奸盜屏跡，曆貝州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang, he was Patrol Commissioner of Fu Prefecture; rogues and thieves vanished from his tracks, and he served successively as Prefect of Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he was patrol commissioner of Fu Prefecture, where thieves disappeared from his jurisdiction, and he later served as prefect of Bei.

sentences.zh: 未幾，請製置慶州鹽池，逐年出絹十萬匹，米十萬斛，遂以廷琬為慶州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long, he requested to administer the salt ponds of Qing Prefecture, annually delivering one hundred thousand bolts of silk and one hundred thousand hu of grain; thereupon Tingwan was made Defense Commissioner of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he petitioned to take charge of Qing Prefecture's salt ponds, promising an annual tribute of one hundred thousand bolts of silk and one hundred thousand hu of grain, and was appointed defense commissioner of Qing.

sentences.zh: 俾製置之，由是嚴刑峻法，屢撓邊人。

translations.literal: He was made to administer them; from this he employed harsh punishments and severe laws, repeatedly troubling the border people.
translations.idiomatic: Once placed in charge, he imposed harsh laws that repeatedly harassed the border population.

sentences.zh: 課利不集，詔移任於金州。

translations.literal: The levied profits did not accumulate; an edict transferred his appointment to Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the expected revenues failed to materialize, an edict transferred him to Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 廷琬據慶州叛，詔邠州節度使李敬周率兵討平之，夷其族。

translations.literal: Tingwan held Qing Prefecture and rebelled; an edict ordered Bin Prefecture Military Governor Li Jingzhou to lead troops to suppress and pacify him, and his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Tingwan seized Qing Prefecture and rebelled. Li Jingzhou, military governor of Bin, was ordered to crush the revolt, and Tingwan's entire clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 張虔釗，遼州人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Qianzhao was a man of Liao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianzhao was from Liao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: （《九國志》云：虔釗，遼州榆社人。

translations.literal: (The 《Records of the Nine States》 says: Qianzhao was a man of Yushe in Liao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Records of the Nine States》 says Qianzhao was from Yushe in Liao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父簡，唐檢校尚書左僕射。）〉

translations.literal: His father Jian was Tang Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian had served as Tang acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉

sentences.zh: 初為太原牙校，以武勇聞於流輩，武皇、莊宗之世，累補左右突騎軍使。

translations.literal: He first served as a military aide at Taiyuan, renowned among his peers for martial valor; in the eras of the Martial Emperor and Emperor Zhuangzong, he was repeatedly appointed Chief of the Left and Right Shock Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a military aide at Taiyuan and won fame among his peers for courage. Under the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong he rose repeatedly to command the imperial shock cavalry.

sentences.zh: （《九國志》：莊宗嘗以偏師取鎮陽，命虔釗率騎為先鋒，屢挫賊銳，遂陷其城。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Records of the Nine States》: Zhuangzong once took Zhenyang with a detached force, ordered Qianzhao to lead the cavalry as vanguard, repeatedly blunted the enemy's edge, and thereby stormed the city.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Records of the Nine States》: When Zhuangzong took Zhenyang with a detached column, he made Qianzhao cavalry vanguard. Qianzhao repeatedly broke the enemy's strength and finally captured the city.)〉

sentences.zh: 明宗素聞虔釗有將帥才，及即位，擢為護駕親軍都指揮使，領春州刺史。

translations.literal: Mingzong had long heard that Qianzhao possessed the talent of a general; when he took the throne, he promoted him to Chief Commander of the Imperial Escort Guard, concurrently holding the post of Prefect of Chun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had long heard of Qianzhao's generalship. On his accession he made him chief commander of the imperial escort guard and prefect of Chun.

sentences.zh: 天成中，與諸將圍王都於中山，大敗契丹於嘉山之下，及定州平，以功授滄州節度使。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng, together with the generals he besieged Wang Du at Zhongshan, greatly defeated the Khitan below Jia Mountain, and when Ding Prefecture was pacified, for his merit was appointed Military Governor of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he joined the generals besieging Wang Du at Zhongshan and routed the Khitan below Jia Mountain. When Dingzhou fell, he was rewarded with the military governorship of Cang.

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》：虔釗鎮滄州日，因亢旱民饑，發廩賑之，方上聞，帝甚嘉獎。

translations.literal: (The 《Idle Talk from Northern Dreams》: When Qianzhao governed Cang Prefecture, because of severe drought the people were starving; he opened the granaries to relieve them. The report had just reached the court when the emperor greatly praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Idle Talk from Northern Dreams》: While governing Cang, Qianzhao opened the granaries during a severe drought to feed the starving people. The emperor praised him warmly when the report arrived.

sentences.zh: 他日秋成，倍鬥征斂，朝論鄙之。）〉

translations.literal: Another day, when the autumn harvest came in, he doubled the grain levies; court opinion despised him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: But when harvest came he doubled the grain levies, and court opinion turned against him.)〉

sentences.zh: 移鎮徐州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長興中，為山南西道節度使兼西面馬步軍都部署。

translations.literal: During Changxing, he was Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit, concurrently Grand Deployer of the Western Horse and Foot Forces.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he became military governor of Shannan West Circuit and grand deployer of the western horse-and-foot forces.

sentences.zh: 及末帝起於鳳翔，閔帝詔令虔釗帥部兵會王師於岐下。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor rose at Fengxiang, Emperor Min issued an edict ordering Qianzhao to lead his troops to join the royal army below Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor rose at Fengxiang, Emperor Min ordered Qianzhao to lead his troops to join the imperial army at Qi.

sentences.zh: 洎西師俱變，虔釗憤惋，退歸興元，因與洋州節度使孫漢韶俱送款於蜀。

translations.literal: When the western armies all turned, Qianzhao was resentful and aggrieved, withdrew to Xingyuan, and together with Yang Prefecture Military Governor Sun Hanshao both sent pledges of allegiance to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the western armies all defected, Qianzhao, bitter and aggrieved, withdrew to Xingyuan and, with Sun Hanshao of Yang Prefecture, submitted to Shu.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥待之尤厚，偽授本鎮節度使，俾知祥坐獲山南之地，由虔釗之故也。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang treated him with exceptional generosity, falsely invested him as military governor of his former command, and enabled Zhixiang to obtain the lands of Shannan without effort—it was because of Qianzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang treated him generously, confirmed him in his former command, and thereby gained Shannan without a fight—largely thanks to Qianzhao.

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》：入蜀，取人產業，黷貨無厭，蜀民怨之。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Idle Talk from Northern Dreams》: Entering Shu, he seized people's estates, was insatiable in corrupt gain, and the Shu people resented him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Idle Talk from Northern Dreams》: In Shu he seized people's property, took bribes without limit, and earned the people's hatred.)〉

sentences.zh: 孟昶嗣偽位，加檢校太師、兼中書令。

translations.literal: When Meng Chang succeeded to the bogus throne, he was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Chang succeeded to the Shu throne, Qianzhao was made acting grand preceptor and concurrent director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，蜀人聞契丹入洛，令虔釗率眾數萬，將寇秦、雍。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin Kaixyun, the Shu people heard the Khitan had entered Luoyang and ordered Qianzhao to lead several tens of thousands, intending to raid Qin and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jin Kaixyun, hearing that the Khitan had entered Luoyang, Shu ordered Qianzhao to lead tens of thousands against Qin and Yong.

sentences.zh: 俄聞漢高祖已定中原，虔釗無功而退。

translations.literal: Shortly they heard the Han Founder had secured the Central Plains; Qianzhao withdrew without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the Han founder had secured the Central Plains, and Qianzhao withdrew without success.

sentences.zh: （《九國志》云：曆左右匡聖馬步軍都指揮使，出為昭武軍節度使。

translations.literal: (The 《Records of the Nine States》 says: He successively served as Chief Commander of the Left and Right Imperial Guard Horse and Foot Forces, then went out as Military Governor of Zhaowu Army.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Records of the Nine States》 says he served as chief commander of the left and right imperial guard forces, then became military governor of Zhaowu.

sentences.zh: 及漢祖即位，乃移鎮梁州，以觀朝廷之變。

translations.literal: When the Han Founder took the throne, he was then transferred to govern Liang Prefecture to observe changes at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder took the throne, he was transferred to Liang Prefecture to watch how the court developed.

sentences.zh: 會晉昌軍節度使趙匡讚、鳳翔節度使侯益俱謀歸蜀，遂以虔釗為北面行營招討使，應接經營。

translations.literal: It happened that Jinchang Army Military Governor Zhao Kuangzan and Fengxiang Military Governor Hou Yi both plotted to return to Shu; Qianzhao was thereupon made Northern Campaign Pacification Commissioner to receive and manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Kuangzan of Jinchang and Hou Yi of Fengxiang both plotted to defect to Shu, Qianzhao was made northern campaign pacification commissioner to coordinate the effort.

sentences.zh: 俄而趙匡讚、侯益請昶出師，掠定三秦，因命虔釗與韓保貞等總師五萬出散關，雄武軍節度使何重建出隴右，奉鑾肅衛都虞候李廷珪出子午穀，會於雍州。

translations.literal: Shortly Zhao Kuangzan and Hou Yi requested Chang to send out the army, seize and settle the Three Qins; thereupon Qianzhao with Han Baozhen and others were ordered to command fifty thousand troops out through San Pass, Xiongwu Army Military Governor He Chongjian out through Longyou, Imperial Escort Purification Guard Chief Adjutant Li Tinggui out through Ziwu Valley, to meet at Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhao and Hou asked Chang to march, conquer the Three Qins, and ordered Qianzhao and Han Baozhen to lead fifty thousand men through San Pass, He Chongjian of Xiongwu through Longyou, and Li Tinggui through Ziwu Valley to converge on Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 廷珪始出子午穀，聞匡讚為王景崇所逼，棄城自拔東去，遂先退師。

translations.literal: Tinggui had just emerged from Ziwu Valley when he heard Kuangzan was pressed by Wang Jingchong, abandoned the city and withdrew east on his own, and therefore first withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui had barely left Ziwu Valley when he learned Kuangzan was besieged by Wang Jingchong, abandoned his position, and withdrew east—so his column retreated first.

sentences.zh: 時虔釗、福誠、保貞師次陳倉，謀不相葉，而侯益聞匡讚已去，廷珪班師，亦誠款中變，閉壘不出。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of Qianzhao, Fucheng, and Baozhen halted at Chencang, their plans not supporting one another; Hou Yi heard Kuangzan had already gone and Tinggui had withdrawn his army, and his sincere pledge also changed midway—he closed his ramparts and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhao, Fucheng, and Baozhen halted at Chencang with divided plans. When Hou Yi learned Kuangzan had fled and Tinggui had withdrawn, he too abandoned his pledge, shut his fort, and refused to march out.

sentences.zh: 司天監趙廷樞累以雲氣不利為諷，保貞乃與福誠率所部取隴州道，會重建歸蜀，虔釗留寶雞，以勢孤不可深入，遂班師。）〉

translations.literal: Director of Astronomy Zhao Tingshu repeatedly used inauspicious cloud signs as indirect admonition; Baozhen then with Fucheng led their units by the Long Prefecture route, met Chongjian returning to Shu; Qianzhao remained at Baoji, deeming his position isolated and unable to penetrate deeply, and thereupon withdrew the army.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The director of astronomy Zhao Tingshu repeatedly cited ill omens in the clouds. Baozhen and Fucheng led their troops toward Long Prefecture, He Chongjian returned to Shu, and Qianzhao, left isolated at Baoji, judged the position untenable and withdrew.)〉

sentences.zh: 行至興州，感憤而卒。

translations.literal: When he reached Xing Prefecture, he died from indignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Xing Prefecture and died of grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 楊彥溫，汴州人，本梁朝之小校也。

translations.literal: Yang Yanwen was a man of Bian Prefecture, originally a petty officer of the Liang court.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yanwen of Bianzhou had begun as a petty officer of the Liang.

sentences.zh: 莊宗朝，累遷裨將。

translations.literal: In the Zhuangzong reign, he was repeatedly promoted to lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong he rose repeatedly to field officer.

sentences.zh: 天成中，為河中副指揮使，及末帝鎮河中，尤善待之，因奏為衙內都指揮使。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng, he was Deputy Commander of Hezhong; when the Last Emperor governed Hezhong he was especially well treated, and thereupon was memorialized as Chief Commander of the Inner Yamen Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he was deputy commander at Hezhong. When the Last Emperor governed there he favored Yanwen and had him named chief of the inner yamen guard.

sentences.zh: 長興元年四月，乘末帝閱馬於黃龍莊，據城謀叛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Changxing, taking advantage of the Last Emperor's horse review at Yellow Dragon Manor, he seized the city and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Changxing, while the Last Emperor was reviewing horses at Yellow Dragon Manor, Yanwen seized the city and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 末帝遣人詰之曰：「吾善待汝，何苦為叛？

translations.literal: The Last Emperor sent a man to interrogate him, saying: "I have treated you well—why must you rebel?
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor sent someone to demand, "I have treated you well. Why rebel?

sentences.zh: 」彥溫報曰：「某非敢負恩，緣奉樞密院宣頭，令某拒命，請相公但歸朝廷。

translations.literal: " Yanwen replied: "I dare not betray your kindness; it is because I received the Bureau of Military Affairs' written order commanding me to refuse obedience—I ask Your Excellency only to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanwen replied, "I do not mean to betray you. I obeyed a written order from the Bureau of Military Affairs to refuse your command. I ask only that you return to court.

sentences.zh: 」數日，詔末帝歸朝。

translations.literal: " Within several days, an edict ordered the Last Emperor to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: " Within days an edict ordered the Last Emperor back to court.

sentences.zh: 明宗疑其詐，不欲興兵，授彥溫絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Mingzong suspected deception and did not wish to raise troops; he appointed Yanwen Prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong suspected a ruse and declined to send troops, appointing Yanwen prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 安重誨堅請出師，即命西京留守索自通、侍衛步軍指揮使藥彥稠等帥兵攻之。

translations.literal: An Chonghui firmly requested sending out the army; he thereupon ordered Western Capital Regent Suo Zitong, Palace Guard Foot Commander Yao Yanchou, and others to lead troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui insisted on military action and ordered Western Capital regent Suo Zitong, palace guard foot commander Yao Yanchou, and others to attack.

sentences.zh: 五日而拔，自閉門及敗，凡十三日。

translations.literal: In five days they stormed it; from closing the gates to defeat, altogether thirteen days.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell in five days; from the closing of the gates to defeat, thirteen days in all.

sentences.zh: 初，彥稠出師，明宗戒之曰：「與朕生致彥溫，吾將自訊之。

translations.literal: At first, when Yanchou set out, Mingzong admonished him: "Bring Yanwen to me alive—I will question him myself.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yanchou marched, Mingzong warned him, "Bring Yanwen to me alive. I will question him myself.

sentences.zh: 」 及收城，斬首傳送，明宗深怒彥稠等。

translations.literal: " When the city was taken, his head was cut off and sent; Mingzong was deeply angry with Yanchou and the others.
translations.idiomatic: " When the city fell they sent his severed head instead, and Mingzong was furious with Yanchou and his officers.

sentences.zh: 時議者以當時四海恬然，五兵載戢，蒲非邊郡，近在國門，而彥溫安敢狂悖。

translations.literal: Commentators of the time held that the four seas were then tranquil, the five weapons sheathed; Pu was no border prefecture but lay close to the capital gates—how could Yanwen dare such madness?
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries noted that the realm was at peace and arms were sheathed, that Pu was no frontier but lay at the capital's doorstep—how could Yanwen dare such recklessness?

sentences.zh: 皆以為安重誨方弄國權，尤忌末帝之名，故巧作窺圖，究莫能傾陷也。

translations.literal: All believed An Chonghui was then manipulating state power and especially feared the Last Emperor's reputation; therefore he craftily made designs of observation, yet in the end could not overthrow him.
translations.idiomatic: Many believed An Chonghui was manipulating state power and feared the Last Emperor's standing, and had engineered the affair to undermine him—yet failed to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 彥溫愚昧，為人所嗾，故滅其族焉。

translations.literal: Yanwen was ignorant and stupid, incited by others; therefore his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwen was a fool used by others, and his clan was destroyed for it.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：《春秋傳》云：「夫不令之臣，天下之所惡也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The 《Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals》 says: "Unworthy ministers are what all under Heaven detests.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: The 《Zuo Commentary》 says, "Unworthy ministers are hated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 」故不復較其優劣焉。

translations.literal: " Therefore I do not again compare their relative merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: " I therefore do not rank them by relative merit.

sentences.zh: 唯虔釗因避地以偷生，彥溫乃為人之所嗾，比諸叛臣，亦可矜也。

translations.literal: Only Qianzhao, because he fled the land to preserve his life, and Yanwen, because he was incited by others—compared with other rebel ministers, may also be pitied.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhao fled only to survive, and Yanwen was another man's tool; compared with other rebels, both deserve some pity.
